thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: ILB healthcheck failures detected for private-vpc-eu1 (control-plane egress errors). 30% of ILB backends flapped in last 3m. Possible downstream observability egress rate limiting. https://goto.redwood/incident/2108765432 :rotating_light:

alex-m (oncall): acked — I'm on it. Paging networking and SRE. If this is egress->obs vendor we may see route suppression across regions. I'll start triage, @emily-cs can you pre-draft a CS blurb?

pagerduty-bot: Incident 35921 acknowledged by alex-m (oncall) — escalation to L2 triggered.

ajay-n: looking. Can someone paste the recent ILB healthcheck logs? I want to check the 502/timeout pattern.

alex-m (oncall): past 10m from logs (filtering for private-vpc-eu1):
```
2026-03-15T12:03:07Z ilb-check healthcheck failed backend-xyz code=503 target=10.2.5.14
2026-03-15T12:03:09Z ilb-check healthcheck failed backend-abc code=504 timeout 15s
2026-03-15T12:03:23Z ilb-check healthcheck ok backend-xyz latency=120ms
2026-03-15T12:04:01Z ilb-check healthcheck failed backend-def code=502 upstream=obs-proxy.redwood-observability.net
```
Looks like failed egress to obs proxy.

sam-net: confirmed on control-plane side we're seeing outcalls to the observability ingest endpoint returning 429s and then GCP ILB healthchecks hit their failure window, triggering routing suppression for some node pools. I've put a filter on gcp vpc flow logs to capture src->obs egress.

ajay-n: hypothesis: our observability agent (third-party) is hitting a vendor-side rate limiter on their public endpoint, causing intermittent connection resets. Those resets are leaking into healthcheck path because we run our healthcheck probe through the same egress NAT path in the Private VPC. If vendor blocks our egress, ILB backend health goes flappy and GCP suppresses route fanout cross-region.

emily-cs: drafting customer note: "We are investigating increased request errors for customers using Private VPC EU region. Root cause appears to be third-party observability vendor rate limits affecting control-plane egress. We're working on mitigation and will update in 30m." Shall I include an ETA?

alex-m (oncall): yes include 30-45m ETA for next update. Mitigation plan I'm executing now:
- open emergency bypass for healthchecks to use local internal probe endpoint (avoid obs egress)
- roll a temporary ip-masq rule to route obs ingestion through dedicated egress nat in us-central1 (less impacted)
- contact observability vendor support and attach rate-limit logs and request immediate relief
- prepare canary routing to failover eu -> us for affected customers if suppression continues

ajay-n: executing step 1: adding local probe endpoint to healthcheck config (makes ILB probe hit localhost health port instead of egress path). Command:```gcloud compute health-checks update http ilb-eu-probe --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8080``` Applying now.

sam-net: applied ip-masq nat rule to force obs egress via dedicated nat in us-central1 for the private-vpc-eu1 subnets. This will add ~90ms RTT for observability, but should stop vendor-side 429s from EU pool.

incident-bot: Note: postmortem checklist item created -> incident/35921/triage. Assigned to ajay-n and maria-sre.

ajay-n: vendor contacted — support ticket #OBS-11234 opened. They see increased request rate from our eu NAT IP and acknowledged soft rate-limiting. Vendor says they can temporarily bump limits for 30m if we provide IPs and request. Sharing IP list in channel.

alex-m (oncall): good. I've kicked the canary failover plan to switch routing for the most impacted customer group (cid: CUST-42) to us-central1. This is a targeted route override, not full failover. Doing it manually now:```kubectl annotate service foo --overwrite rollout-region=us-central1``` Monitoring.

emily-cs: updating customers: posted to CUST-42 slack and support queue. Note included mitigation and ETA.

maria-sre: joining handoff — been paged. Quick check: any downstream alerts from telemetry that would indicate persistent token storms or auth issues?

ajay-n: saw a short burst of OAuth errors as well (observation vendor proxy returned 401 for some requests when it rate-limited). We rotated the agent token as a precaution for a subset of nodes.

sam-net: traffic steady after NAT change, no new 429s to vendor from eu pool in last 3m. ILB health stabilized for 80% of backends. We're still monitoring for churn.

alex-m (oncall): current impact summary for timeline note: 2026-03-15T12:00Z - partial backend flapping in private-vpc-eu1 caused by vendor-side egress rate limits -> control-plane healthcheck failures -> GCP route suppression for a subset of cross-region fanout. Mitigation applied: local probe reconfiguration + nat reroute + targeted canary region override. Customer impact: transient increased 5xx errors for customers routed to affected backends (approx 6 customers, highest severity CUST-42).

maria-sre: I'll take ownership for the next 2h and complete the postmortem root-cause analysis. alex-m, if you need me to keep the vendor chase, I can. Handing off oncall to maria-sre.

alex-m (oncall): handing off. I'm clear and leaving notes in the incident doc. Maria, assigned to you for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident 35921 reassigned to maria-sre.

emily-cs: updated public status page and support tickets. Will standby for postmortem blurb.

incident-bot: REMINDER: please add runbook updates if we want to avoid using obs egress for healthchecks in Private VPCs going forward.

maria-sre: adding runbook item now: prefer local probe host for ILBs in Private VPC, and maintain dedicated NAT pool for obs egress to avoid cross-region suppression. Also adding a test to simulate vendor 429s in staging.

alex-m (oncall): thanks team. Closing active mitigation. Monitor windows: 30m.

emily-cs: note: customers notified, CUST-42 confirmed reduced error rates after failover.

incident-bot: Incident 35921 status -> mitigated. Postmortem owner: maria-sre.
